# Research

> Structured AI-driven research sessions. Design research structures, conduct interactive Q&A sessions, manage tasks, build visual roadmaps, create cross-referenced knowledge entries, and track progress.

## Data Model

```
Research (R1, R2...) — statuses: active, completed, archived
  |-- Section (S1, S2...) — logical topics within a research
  |     |-- Entry (E1, E2...) — markdown documents with findings
  |
  |-- Session (SS1, SS2...) — interactive Q&A interview (multiple per research)
  |     |-- Question (Q1, Q2...) — structured prompts with answers
  |
  |-- Task (T1, T2...) — todo items for tracking work
  |
  |-- Roadmap (RM1, RM2...) — visual graphs for learning paths, strategy maps, step-by-step guides
  |     |-- Node (N1, N2...) — graph nodes with type, status, and content
  |     |-- Edge — directed connections between nodes with labels
  |
  Entry -?-> Session — optional link (session_id tracks which session produced the entry)
  Entry --[[E3]]--> Entry — cross-references form a knowledge graph
  Entry --[[RM1]]--> Roadmap — cross-references to roadmaps and nodes
```

Cross-references work in entry content, question text, question answers, task results, and session notes. They are rendered as clickable links in the web UI and stored in the `crossrefs` table for graph queries.

Entries come in two kinds, chosen with `entry_type`: `markdown` (default) and `blocks` — an article of typed blocks (paragraph, heading, list, table, quote, code, callout, divider, image, html) that mixes prose with alerts and custom visuals. The `html` block holds a self-contained HTML document rendered in a sandboxed iframe at full height, for charts and interactive layouts; `entry_type: artifact` is sugar for a document holding one of them. See [Block Documents](/llms/blocks.md).

Content supports Mermaid diagrams via fenced code blocks with `mermaid` language. All Mermaid diagram types are supported (flowchart, sequence, class, state, ER, Gantt, pie, mindmap, timeline, etc.). Diagrams are rendered as interactive SVG in the web UI. See [MCP Client Guide](/llms/mcp-client-guide.md) for examples.

| Syntax | Target | Example |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `[[E3]]` | Entry in same research | Links to entry E3 |
| `[[R2:E5]]` | Entry in another research | Links to entry E5 in research R2 |
| `[[R2]]` | Research | Links to research R2 |
| `[[RM1]]` | Roadmap | Links to roadmap RM1 |
| `[[RM1:N3]]` | Roadmap node | Links to roadmap RM1 (node N3 context) |

A research can have **multiple sessions** (e.g. initial exploration, deep-dive, follow-up). Each session has its own set of questions. Sessions are displayed grouped in the mindmap and listed on the research detail page.

## Docs

- [MCP Client Guide](/llms/mcp-client-guide.md): Practical guide for AI assistants interacting via MCP tools. Covers all 32 tools, the input-schema contract (every property required, which ones accept `null`), content formatting (newlines, markdown, cross-references), entry types, roadmap node types, entity references, common pitfalls, and where short codes are accepted. Start here if you are an MCP client.
- [Domain Guide](/llms/domain-guide.md): Complete reference for every entity (Research, Section, Entry, Session, Question, Task, Roadmap, CrossRef). Describes fields, statuses, relationships, lifecycle, and when to use each entity. Includes tagging strategy, cross-reference syntax, and tips.
- [Conducting Research](/llms/conducting-research.md): Step-by-step guide on how to initialize, conduct, and complete a research project. Interview workflow, entry creation with cross-references, task tracking, roadmap creation, and best practices.
- [Tasks](/llms/tasks.md): Guide to using tasks for tracking work items, action items, and outcomes within a research. When to create tasks, statuses, priorities, tasks vs questions, and best practices.
- [Roadmaps](/llms/roadmaps.md): Guide to building visual directed graphs — learning paths, strategy maps, decision trees. When to create roadmaps, node/edge types, custom statuses by domain, how to build a graph step by step, and best practices.
- [Block Documents](/llms/blocks.md): The `blocks` entry type — the JSON document shape, the catalog of all 10 block types with every field and cap, how text fields carry inline markdown and cross-references, the sandboxed `html` block, title/description derivation, the `artifact` alias, and what export and import do with a block document. Read this before writing an entry with `entry_type: blocks`.
- [Export](/llms/export.md): How to export a whole research or a single session as markdown or PDF, plus the portable JSON export/import format. Endpoint reference, web UI export pages, and how block documents are carried through each export.
- [REST API — OpenAPI Specification](/api/openapi.yaml): OpenAPI 3.1 spec with request/response schemas. It covers the core read and write endpoints but lags the router — export, import, graph and link endpoints are missing from it, so treat the guides above (and `internal/api/server.go`) as authoritative for route existence.
